**Given:** the choice assumptions, fixed covariant model, three explicit reduction hypotheses, and complete constrained smooth data in the Statement.

[L1] The metric wave reduction is [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]]. The actual compact-state periodic existence and smoothness suppliers are [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]], [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] and [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

[L2] With conserved stress on a reduced solution, vanishing initial $H$ and the normal constraint residuals give zero normal derivative of $H$, and the homogeneous subsidiary wave equation forces $H=0$ and the full Einstein equations ([[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]], [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]).

[L3] For the same fixed model, complete initialization and coefficient family as here, physical wave-coordinate comparison gives local geometric uniqueness; future isometries fixing the initial patch agree as germs by preservation of its normal geodesics ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]]). Normal geodesic maps and the inverse function theorem are [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] and [[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]].

[L4] Countable relatively compact coordinate refinements, locally finite shrinkings and smooth subordinate partitions are [[lem-every-open-cover-of-a-manifold-has-a-countable-cover-by-relatively-compact-coordinate-balls-subordinate-to-it]], [[lem-a-countable-coordinate-ball-cover-has-a-countable-locally-finite-shrinking]] and [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]].

[L5] The local cone-energy estimate uses [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] and [[thm-gronwall-integral-inequality]]. A smooth embedded spacelike surface has an intrinsic variable-width temporal collar, whose interior domain of dependence has that surface Cauchy and is globally hyperbolic ([[lem-gr-local-cauchy-neighborhood]] clause (d)).



1.1 (Complete harmonic initial value.) On a small initial coordinate ball set $g_{00}=-1$, $g_{0i}=0$, $g_{ij}=h_{ij}$, $p_{ij}=2K_{ij}$ and $q_{abi}=\partial_i g^0_{ab}$. For the flat comparison metric the Christoffel contraction at the surface is $$H^0=\tfrac12p_{00}+\operatorname{tr}_hK,\qquad H^\ell=-h^{\ell i}p_{0i}+h^{jk}\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{jk}.$$ Thus prescribe $p_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK$ and $p_{0i}=h_{i\ell}h^{jk}\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{jk}$, giving $H=0$ initially. The spatial derivative definitions and the initialization $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$ supply every remaining initial value and every auxiliary compatibility constraint. In this coordinate gauge $\partial_0=n$ initially, so $K_{ij}=\tfrac12p_{ij}$ and the reconstructed matter data are exactly $d$. The generally nonzero $p_{0i}$ is essential for the flat comparison metric; the special background $-dt^2+h$ instead gives $p_{0i}=0$. [given, L1, algebra]

2.1 (Local coupled reduced existence.) Shrink about each initial point so the initial state values lie in a compact ball strictly inside a convex admissible state ball $O_*\Subset O$. Extend the smooth data to a torus by a spatial cutoff interpolating to a fixed value in $O_*$; convexity keeps all interpolated values admissible. On a smaller initial cylinder extend the coefficient functions by a smooth spatial cutoff, keeping the original functions on the smaller patch and interpolating $A^0$ to the identity, $A^i$ to zero and $B$ to zero outside the larger patch. Symmetry persists and the convex positive-matrix cone preserves positivity. Choose compact sets $C\subset\operatorname{int}C'\Subset O_*$ containing the extended data and a finite $H^s$ norm bound $R$ for one integer $s\ge5$. On the compact time, spatial and state ranges the coefficient derivatives are bounded and $A^0\ge aI$ for some $a>0$. These are the actual hypotheses of [L1]; the periodic existence and smooth persistence theorems give a smooth solution on a nonzero interval. Restrict to the original patch, where it solves the original coupled system. No theorem for a prescribed spacetime tensor $T$ has been substituted for this coupled existence argument. [step 1.1, given, L1, construct]

3.1 (Removal of extensions.) For two smooth solutions of systems agreeing near a smaller initial cone, subtract their equations and put $v=z_1-z_2$. On a smaller compact cylinder their states lie in a common convex admissible compact neighborhood. The coefficient mean-value formula gives $$A^\mu(x,z_1)\partial_\mu v+C(x)v=0,$$ where $C$ includes the bounded terms obtained from coefficient differences multiplying $\partial_\mu z_2$ and from the source difference. Let $b=\sup_{|\xi|=1}\|\sum_i\xi_iA^i(x,z_1)\|$ there and choose $\lambda>b/a$. On the shrinking ball of radius $r-\lambda t$, [L5] gives $$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{B_{r-\lambda t}}v^{\mathsf T}A^0v\le c\int_{B_{r-\lambda t}}v^{\mathsf T}A^0v-\int_{\partial B_{r-\lambda t}}v^{\mathsf T}(\lambda A^0+\nu_iA^i)v\le c\int_{B_{r-\lambda t}}v^{\mathsf T}A^0v.$$ The boundary matrix is positive since $\lambda a>b$. Equal initial values give zero energy by Gronwall. Reverse time for the other half. This proves independence of the extensions on an actual open initial neighborhood, with the combined spatial-symbol bound rather than an incorrect bound on each separate $A^i$. [step 2.1, L5, algebra]

3.2 (Recovery without circularity.) By hypothesis 2, the auxiliary constraints propagate and the reconstructed reduced solution solves the original matter equations, giving the exact initial stress and data. Hypothesis 3 therefore gives $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on this reduced solution before Einstein recovery. Its initial geometric jet gives $H=0$ by step 1.1 and the Gauss-Codazzi constraint equations give $E(n,n)=E(n,e_i)=0$. On a reduced solution one has $E_{ab}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a-g_{ab}\nabla_cH^c)$; since tangential derivatives of $H$ vanish initially, this reads $E_{00}=\tfrac12\nabla_0H_0$ and $E_{0i}=\tfrac12\nabla_0H_i$ in the initial orthogonal frame. Thus $\nabla_nH=0$ initially. Conservation gives the homogeneous subsidiary equation and [L2] forces $H=0$, hence $E=0$, on a smaller neighborhood. The local solution is now a full physical development. [step 1.1, step 2.1, given, L2, algebra]

4.1 (Common normal collar representatives.) For each local full development define $E_i(s,p)=\exp_{j_i(p)}(sn_i(p))$. Its differential at $(0,p)$ is $(c,V)\mapsto cn_i+dj_i(V)$, an isomorphism. The inverse function theorem [L3] gives, after local shrinking, an injective normal collar over a smaller initial ball. Pull its metric and matter fields back to its normal domain in $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$. If two initial balls intersect, [L3] gives a future data-fixing isometry germ on the intersection. Its differential is the identity on the slice tangent directions and sends $n_i$ to $n_j$ by uniqueness of the future unit normal. Preservation and uniqueness of affinely parametrized geodesics give $$\Phi(E_i(s,p))=E_j(s,p)$$ for every sufficiently small segment staying in its domain. Consequently the two pulled-back full fields agree on an open neighborhood of the zero section over the intersection. This uses uniqueness of isometry germs and normal parametrization; fixing the slice alone does not make a general map the identity off it. No geometric uniqueness is used to create the reduced solution or to propagate its constraints. [step 3.2, L3, construct]

5.1 (Locally finite literal patching.) Choose [L4]'s countable locally finite shrinking $\overline{W_i}=K_i\subset V_i\subset\overline{V_i}\subset O_i$, with $O_i$ normal-collar existence patches from step 4.1 and $K_i$ compact. Each $K_i$ meets only finitely many $K_j$, since $(V_j)$ is locally finite and $K_j\subset V_j$. Compactness supplies $t_i>0$ for which the $i$th normal representative exists on $(-t_i,t_i)\times K_i$. On each nonempty compact $K_i\cap K_j$, step 4.1 supplies an open equality neighborhood; a finite subcover gives a symmetric width $t_{ij}=t_{ji}>0$ on which the representatives agree over that compact intersection. Countable Choice selects widths for the countably many indices and pairs. Set $$\delta_i=\tfrac12\min\bigl(\{t_i\}\cup\{t_{ij}:K_i\cap K_j\ne\varnothing\}\bigr)>0.$$ The minimum is finite. The normal representatives agree on every overlap of $(-\delta_i,\delta_i)\times W_i$ and so define single smooth tensor fields on their literal open union $\Omega\subset\mathbb R\times\Sigma$. Ordinary equality supplies the triple-overlap cocycle, with no quotient construction or Hausdorffness issue. For a subordinate locally finite partition $(\rho_i)$ set $\alpha(p)=\tfrac12\sum_i\delta_i\rho_i(p)>0$. At each point the finite weighted average is at most the largest active width, whose $W_i$ contains that point; hence $\{|s|<\alpha(p)\}\subset\Omega$. Restriction gives a smooth positive variable-width collar and the exact full data. No positive uniform lower bound is required. [step 4.1, L4, given, construct]

6.1 (Causal neighborhood and uniqueness.) Apply [L5]'s generic embedded-spacelike clause to the surface $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in this glued development. It furnishes a further temporal variable-width collar $U$ and an open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(\Sigma)\cup D^-_U(\Sigma))$ containing the entire initial surface, where $\Sigma$ is Cauchy and $W$ is globally hyperbolic. The domains are intrinsic to $U$; no assertion that the one-sided domain itself is open is needed. Finally the fixed model, same reconstruction and complete data meet all hypotheses of [L3]'s uniqueness theorem. Two full developments are therefore isometric near the whole initial surface, matching all matter fields and future orientation. These are the asserted existence, causal and uniqueness conclusions. [step 5.1, given, L3, L5] ∎

**Given:** Countable Choice, the fixed strict EOS and enthalpy reference, the metric and unit future velocity, the chart, and complete fluid data where initialization is claimed.

[L1] $r'=c_s/(\epsilon+p)>0$; the enthalpy change of variables is a smooth diffeomorphism of open intervals ([[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

[L2] Stress divergence decomposes into the energy and Euler equations, using unit normalization, metric compatibility and $\Pi$ projection ([[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]], [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

[L3] The reduced Einstein metric block is symmetric with positive time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ on its admissible chart state ([[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]]).

[L4] The inverse metric and musical operations identify $u^\perp$ as a positive definite three-space, and a timelike covector with $\zeta(u)>0$ has $|\zeta_\perp|<\zeta(u)$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).



1.1 (Equations and conservation.) By [L1], $Dr=c_sD\epsilon/(\epsilon+p)$ and $c_s\partial_ar=p'\partial_a\epsilon/(\epsilon+p)$. Hence division by $\epsilon+p>0$ transforms the energy and Euler equations into the displayed enthalpy system, and the inverse transformation recovers them. Applying [L2] proves equivalence to stress conservation for every metric and normalized velocity, without requiring Einstein's equation. [given, L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 (Actual independent velocity coordinates.) Restrict a chart to the open metric states with $g_{00}<0$ and positive spatial metric block, as holds near its initially orthogonal surface. Use independent components $y^i=u^i$ and set $b=g_{0i}y^i$, $c=g_{ij}y^iy^j$. The future branch of the normalization equation is $$u^0=\frac{-b-\sqrt{b^2-g_{00}(1+c)}}{g_{00}}.$$ The discriminant is positive and $u^0>0$. It is smooth, and differentiating normalization gives $g(u,e_A)=0$ for $e_A=\partial u/\partial y^A$ at fixed metric. The spatial components of $e_A$ are the standard basis, so these three vectors are a smooth basis of $u^\perp$. This parametrizes all future unit velocities in the local chart. Terms from differentiating $u(g,y)$ with respect to $g$ multiply $\partial g$; the connection terms do likewise. When metric first-order variables are appended, all are zeroth-order sources in the full unknowns. [given, L4, algebra, construct]

2.1 (Smooth symmetric coefficient matrices.) In the leading part of step 1.1, $\partial_\mu u=e_B\partial_\mu y^B$ modulo the metric-derivative terms of step 1.2. Multiply the Euler vector equation by $g(e_A,\cdot)$. Its components together with the energy equation have coefficient matrices at $\partial_\mu$ with entries $$A^\mu_{rr}=u^\mu,\qquad A^\mu_{rB}=c_s e_B^\mu=A^\mu_{Br},\qquad A^\mu_{AB}=u^\mu g(e_A,e_B).$$ They are smooth and symmetric, and their covector contraction is exactly $Q_\zeta$ in the Statement. The Euler equation is tangent to $u^\perp$ because unit normalization is enforced, so taking its three $e_A$ components is equivalent to its full vector equation. Thus this is an actual equivalent coordinate system, not only a symbol computed in a different rest frame at each point. [step 1.1, step 1.2, L4, algebra]

3.1 (Positivity and eigenvalues.) For $a=\delta r$ and $v=\delta u\in u^\perp$, [L4] and Cauchy-Schwarz give $|\zeta(v)|\le|\zeta_\perp||v|$ and therefore $$Q_\zeta((a,v),(a,v))\ge\left(\zeta(u)-c_s|\zeta_\perp|\right)(a^2+|v|^2)>0.$$ The strict last inequality uses $c_s<1$ and $|\zeta_\perp|<\zeta(u)$. In a rest orthonormal basis the matrix has diagonal blocks $\zeta(u)$ and $\zeta(u)I_3$ and off-diagonal $c_s\zeta_\perp$. The two directions perpendicular to $\zeta_\perp$ give eigenvalue $\zeta(u)$, and the remaining two-dimensional block gives $\zeta(u)\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$. Thus the actual time matrix for the positively evaluated timelike time conormal is positive; after relatively compact shrinking its lower bound is uniform. [step 2.1, given, L4, algebra]

4.1 (Coupling, complete initialization and recovery.) Append [L3]'s metric block. Stress depends algebraically on $(g,r,y)$; the fluid metric derivatives from step 1.2 depend algebraically on the metric first-order variables, so the combined principal matrices remain block diagonal and symmetric. The time block is positive by step 3.1 and [L3]. At the initial orthogonal metric, the prescribed $v_0$ gives the normalized bundle velocity $U_0=W_0(N+v_0)$ and initializes every independent fluid variable as stated. Reconstruction keeps $u$ unit and future; the smooth inverse enthalpy map and step 2.1 recover the full fluid equations on any reduced solution. Step 1.1 then gives conserved stress on that reduced metric before imposing Einstein recovery. Conversely every physical fluid solution transforms to these same equations and variables. All asserted conclusions follow. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, L1, L3, algebra] ∎

**Given:** the fixed scalar model, chart, background, admissible metric state, and complete compatible initial scalar data.

[L1] Metric wave reduction and positive symmetric metric block are [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]], with gauge and reduced equation as in [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]].

[L2] The scalar wave equation is $g^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi-g^{ab}\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\partial_c\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$. The Christoffel symbols are smooth algebraic functions of $(g,p,q)$ by metric compatibility and the coordinate connection formula ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]], [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]], [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], [[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

[L3] The scalar stress formula is [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]; its local conservation identity is $\nabla^aT_{ab}=K_\phi(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial_b\varphi$ ([[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]). Only its forward implication is used.



1.1 (Scalar symmetric system.) Write $D_0=P$ and $D_i=Q_i$. Use $\partial_0\varphi=P$, $\partial_0Q_i=\partial_iP$ and $$-g^{00}\partial_0P-2g^{0i}\partial_iP-g^{ij}\partial_iQ_j+g^{ab}\Gamma^c{}_{ab}D_c+V'(\varphi)=0.$$ Multiplying the $Q_i$ equations by $g^{ji}$ gives time block $\operatorname{diag}(1,-g^{00},g^{ij})$. For each spatial derivative $\partial_k$, its $P,P$ entry is $-2g^{0k}$, and its $P,Q_j$ and $Q_j,P$ entries are both $-g^{kj}$; all other scalar spatial entries vanish. Thus all spatial matrices are symmetric and the time matrix is positive definite on the stated open set. The lower terms are smooth functions of $z$ by [L2]. [given, L2, algebra]

2.1 (Compatibility and matter recovery.) The first and third scalar equations imply $\partial_0(Q_i-\partial_i\varphi)=\partial_iP-\partial_i\partial_0\varphi=0$. The prescribed complete data give zero initial residual, so $Q_i=\partial_i\varphi$ throughout the local solution, while $P=\partial_0\varphi$ by its first equation. Substitute these relations in the displayed $P$ equation: it is exactly the scalar wave equation of [L2], multiplied by $-1$. Every physical scalar solution satisfies these equations after extraction. This establishes matter recovery on the reduced metric without using its Einstein residual. [step 1.1, given, L2, algebra]

3.1 (Coupled reduction and initialization.) Append the metric block of [L1]. Its compatibility equations likewise recover the metric derivatives from compatible data; the scalar stress is a smooth algebraic function of $(g,\varphi,P,Q)$ by [L3]. Conversely the scalar connection terms use $(g,p,q)$ without derivatives of those first-order variables. The combined principal matrices are therefore the two symmetric diagonal blocks with no cross derivatives, and the positive time matrices persist on a sufficiently small open state neighborhood. Complete scalar data determine every matter variable as stated, not merely stress tensor jets. Smooth background Christoffel coefficients change $p,q$ to $\bar\nabla_0g,\bar\nabla_ig$ by adding expressions linear in $g$; this invertible zeroth-order change preserves the reduction, with a congruence of principal matrices when changing the equations. [step 1.1, step 2.1, L1, L3, algebra]

4.1 (Conservation on the reduced solution.) Step 2.1 has already recovered the full scalar equation. Applying [L3]'s local identity gives $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on this reduced solution before Einstein recovery. The identity and reduction are local tensor equations, so using local orientations if needed imposes no global orientability restriction. This proves all stated conclusions without a converse from stress conservation to the scalar equation. [step 2.1, step 3.1, L3, algebra] ∎

**Given:** Countable and Dependent Choice and the four branches with their smooth constrained data.

[L1] Reduced local existence and constraint propagation for the vacuum branch ([[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]], [[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]]).

[L2] The fixed-model development and uniqueness theorems require a specified covariant model, its actual coupled symmetric-hyperbolic family, complete compatible initialization and matter recovery/conservation on the reduced solution before Einstein recovery. They apply here to vacuum, scalar and strict fluid; dust uses its independent actual flow/frame theorem ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]], [[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]]).

[L3] The branch theorems verifying the hypotheses and producing the developments: scalar [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]], barotropic fluid [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]], dust [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]].



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Vacuum branch.) There are no matter variables and $T=0$, so matter reconstruction and conservation on the reduced solution are automatic. The metric wave block and complete harmonic jet of [L2] give its reduction and initialization contract; the displayed vacuum constraints give zero initial normal residuals. Applying the vacuum instance of [L2] yields the full solution, intrinsic Cauchy neighborhood and fixed-data future isometry uniqueness, with [L1] giving the reduced-to-full recovery. [given, L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 (Scalar and strict-fluid branches.) Their branch theorems in [L3] verify the complete fixed-model contract, including all initial first-order variables, auxiliary recovery and conservation before Einstein recovery. Apply these concrete theorems to obtain exactly the stated developments and complete-data uniqueness. Local initial values lie in compact admissible state neighborhoods; smooth cutoff extensions have finite $H^s$ norm for each finite integer $s\ge5$, and smooth persistence supplies exactly the smooth branch. No optimal finite-regularity threshold is asserted. [given, L2, L3, algebra]

2.1 (Geodesic dust branch.) Put $\rho_0:=\varepsilon_0/c^2$ and apply [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] to this mass-normalized density and the prescribed $U_0$. Its initial tensor is $\rho_0c^2U_0^\flat\otimes U_0^\flat=\varepsilon_0U_0^\flat\otimes U_0^\flat$, so its constraints are exactly the present constraints. It gives an independent smooth frame-reduction development with its common-flow uniqueness and variable-width patching, without invoking the abstract harmonic matter hypothesis for dust. Recover $\varepsilon=c^2\rho$; constant scaling preserves continuity, geodesic velocity, nonnegativity, the empty-region branch and the stress tensor. Its causal and isometry conclusions are therefore precisely the stated ones. [given, L3, algebra] ∎
